rows.text: Which of the following will NOT be triggered by the release of acetyl choline in the synapse at the neuromuscular junction during muscle contraction?
options: Generation of an action potential in the muscles
Release of \(\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}\) from the sarcoplasmic reticulum
Binding of ATP molecules to the myosin head
Shifting of tropomyosin to expose the myosin binding sites on actin filaments

rows.text:
The diagram below shows a typical ECG.

If the AV node is not functional, which of the following options correctly represents the changes seen in the ECG?

figure.note: A single ECG trace: a small P wave, then the QRS complex (Q dip, tall R peak, S dip), then a broad T wave; peaks labelled P, Q, R, S, T.

options: P wave will sustain longer with smaller amplitude
The QRS complex will be absent
The T wave will sustain longer with smaller amplitude
The distance between the P wave and the QRS complex will be smaller

rows.text:
Listed below are different plant reproductive strategies.
I. Parthenocarpy
II. Syngamy
III. Apomixis
IV. Polyembryony
Which of them can give rise to a clonal progeny having the same genotype as that of the mother plant?
The diagram below represents the pedigree of a certain genetic disease (affected individuals are shaded). What is the mode of inheritance of the gene responsible for this disease?

figure.note: Four-generation pedigree (squares = males, circles = females, filled = affected). Generation I: unaffected male x affected female. Their four children, left to right: affected male; affected female; affected female (married to an unaffected male); affected male (married to an unaffected female). The affected male's couple has an unaffected daughter and an unaffected son. The affected female's couple has an affected son (married to an unaffected female) and an affected daughter (married to an unaffected male). That affected son's children: an unaffected daughter and an unaffected son. That affected daughter's children: two affected sons.

rows.text: An *E. coli* whose DNA is fully labeled by \(\mathrm{^{15}N}\) is grown in a medium containing \(\mathrm{^{14}NH_4Cl}\). What will be the percentage of hybrid (\(\mathrm{^{15}N/^{14}N}\)) and light (\(\mathrm{^{14}N/^{14}N}\)) DNA molecules at the end of 80 minutes (assume that doubling time of *E. coli* is 20 minutes)?

The following plots represent the body size distributions of a fruit fly population. Dashed lines represent the ancestral distributions and continuous lines represent the distributions after a few generations. If the larger individuals have better survival as well as higher reproductive rates, which diagram below best represents the expected change in the distribution of body size (X-axis represents body size while Y-axis represents frequency)?
options: Continuous curve the same shape as the dashed curve but shifted towards smaller body size
Continuous curve with the same mean as the dashed curve but narrower and taller
Continuous curve the same shape as the dashed curve but shifted towards larger body size
Continuous curve with two peaks, one either side of the single dashed peak, dipping at the middle
